items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Sidney Bechet and an unnamed man ('man say', 'he') finding a clarinet and making a reed from 'cane'. The interviewer clarifies the material is 'Cane', but the interviewee does not identify 'Cane' as a person he knows, nor does he claim a personal relationship w

ctx.x: say no. So man say, well he blow, blow on what? And he plays clarinet. Well I got one of them things back up there in the loft, in the garage, I don't know if he can blow it. Been up there for years, just laying up there. Wait, I'll go get it. I used to say, yeah, go get it. This is true, that man went up there and brought that old clarinet back and cobwebs was in it and everything else and he -- key -- couple of keys was off of it. And no reed and therewas one of them places What's you call that -- all that --…

The cane, yeah, one of the canes. Lot of cane growing. Man went back there and cut one of them stalks off there and come out there and Bechet set down there and on that track, and he cut that keys, cut that -- I don't know how he done that, but he did fix the key to put on that clarinet, and cut him out a reed, and put it on there and blowing his head off. Come in there start to blowing, oh Lord, that was it.
